novelty_flags.label: lem:pairwise-identification
novelty_flags.one_line: The clean-comparison identification and weighted-combination conclusion are already covered by Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna's Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.1; retain this only as a supporting reduction.

soundness_flags.label: ass:closed-range
soundness_flags.one_line: Given ass:joint-covariance-spectrum and the definitions of A_P, A_P^*, U_omega, and Sigma_omega, A_PA_P^*v=Sigma_omega^{-1}E[U_omega U_omega'|X]v=v, so closed range and bounded invertibility are automatic.

soundness_flags.label: ass:learner-rates and def:attainment-class
soundness_flags.one_line: The triangular law class is carved by performance of named off-fold learners rather than a law-level estimability property; move procedure-specific bounds to the attainment theorem or quantify them as existence of estimators.

soundness_flags.label: ass:learner-rates
soundness_flags.one_line: Its operative empirical-process, nuisance-product, covariance, and ridge inequalities are only called “displayed” but are not stated, so membership in M_n and the asserted uniform remainder are not determined.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 15–16, Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.1; p. 19, Remark 4.6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4.1 identifies staggered-DDD ATT(g,t) using each valid clean comparison group; Corollary 4.1 permits weights summing to one; Remark 4.6 interprets the resulting constant-weight combination as optimal GMM based on recentered influence functions.
Theorem 3.2 optimally weights valid baseline periods and comparison groups for staggered DiD, and Theorem 4.1 gives an estimator attaining its semiparametric efficiency bound.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 8–9, Theorem 5 and equation (6); p. 9 cross-fitting construction
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives a nonparametric panel-DDD efficient influence function and constructs a cross-fitted nuisance-based estimator for its canonical DDD setting.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Primary full text was inaccessible to fetch; publisher-indexed abstract and metadata at https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/econom/v170y2012i2p442-457.html
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible publication record confirms the journal article computes efficiency bounds for sequential moment restrictions with unknown functions and proposes an optimally weighted orthogonalized sieve minimum-distance estimator; no theorem-text comparison is relied on here.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3 and discussion of K-fold cross-fitting
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article defines cross-fitting as swapping training and estimation samples and discusses its K-fold implementation for orthogonal-score estimation.
The paper describes stacked DDD as a complementary, generally inefficient just-identified GMM construction when control units are shared across stacks.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Write every required learner-rate and empirical-process inequality explicitly, and state the theorem conditionally on those bounds rather than using an undefined “displayed bounds” placeholder.

Replace the procedure-dependent attainment class with law-level sieve approximability and existence-of-estimator conditions; retain the deterministic lexicographic learner as the proposed attaining construction.
Use the identity A_PA_P^*=I implied by the conditional covariance definition to remove ass:closed-range and present the population score directly as q_P-A_P^*A_Pq_P.

Add a theorem-level comparison showing the aggregate variance gain over both the Ortiz-Villavicencio--Sant'Anna constant-GMM estimator and the Chen-Sant'Anna-Xie conditional weighting architecture under an explicit DDD reduction.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision: make the attainment regime mathematically explicit and law-level, remove the redundant closed-range premise, and retain pairwise identification only as published supporting structure.
